episode_title: Batch, Built Right: How Open Platforms Are Rewriting the Rules of Manufacturing Execution

real_qa.q: What is batch processing in manufacturing and why is getting it wrong so costly?
real_qa.r: Batch processing in industrial manufacturing works like a baking analogy: you follow a recipe with known quantities and process steps to turn raw materials into end product with automated process controls and digital recordation. When mistakes occur in batch processing, manufacturers lose not only raw material costs but also the expensive hazmat disposal and time spent mixing. Industries that depend on batch processing include chemical processors, food and beverage, pharmaceuticals, and construction materials.

real_qa.q: How does an open platform approach built on Ignition differ from proprietary batch and MES systems?
real_qa.r: With an open platform like Ignition, solution providers can pick and choose the best technologies to deliver robust solutions and expand capability over time. Proprietary systems create proprietary data silos and are locked in old mentalities and methods that are hard to transfer to younger people. Open platforms allow information created from batch systems to be published in standard format so people can act on issues quicker in real time, enabling tighter tolerances and modern approaches that people understand how to use.
real_qa.requete: open platform batch MES vs proprietary systems

real_qa.q: What is ISA-88 and how does it apply to batch control systems?
real_qa.r: ISA-88 is the gold standard for batch control and is a key standard that allows manufacturers to create standardized approaches. The approach uses standard control modules built in PLC logic that tie through standard interfaces into HMI components and historians. This allows separate components to tie together cleanly, with equipment modules that are standardized and can be deployed rapidly to multiple sites, facilities, and lines with a standard approach to recipe management and control logic.

real_qa.q: How did Polaris Automation help PPG Industries move away from Excel-based scheduling?
real_qa.r: Polaris built a Core Data scheduling module within Ignition that replicated the same functionality as PPG's Excel-based scheduling that was fed from their ERP exports. After iteratively adding more capability as requested, PPG officially went off Excel completely two weeks before the podcast was recorded and now utilizes the scheduler purely within the platform. This transformation took approximately five years in the making with a cross-functional team approach.

real_qa.q: What is the tier board operations approach and how does PPG use it for Kaizen?
real_qa.r: Tier board operations are a true data empowerment technology where PPG operates across tier basis one through five, with operations gathered around tier boards that execute meetings conducted at the same day, time, starting on time and ending on time with the same flow every time. Information ingested through these meetings gets fed into the system and can be used in their Kaizen operations and processes to solve problems that emerge from those discussions.

real_qa.q: Why did Polaris Automation transition from project-based transactional relationships to long-term strategic partnerships with manufacturers?
real_qa.r: Polaris recognized that historically systems from the 90s and 2000s were not set up to support what manufacturers need in the current day and future. Historically the business model was transactional: clients create scope, companies bid, win projects, execute, then support. Now Polaris sees an opportunity and duty as systems integrators to come alongside customers as innovative partners, helping them get outside of the vacuum they operate under and providing hope and encouragement to create clarity out of industry confusion.
real_qa.requete: systems integrator transactional to strategic partnership
